model-validation-s1.title: Residual plots for two models of follower counts
model-validation-s1.text: A new video channel had $210, 262, 330, 410, 515, 640$ and $805$ followers at the end of weeks $t = 0$ to $6$. A linear regression $L$ and an exponential regression $E$ were fit to the data. The plot shows each model's residuals, actual minus predicted: open circles for $L$, filled dots for $E$.

plot.label: Residual plot: open circles for the linear model form a U shape, positive at t = 0, negative from t = 2 to 5, positive at t = 6; filled dots for the exponential model stay close to 0 with no pattern

model-validation-s2.title: Two models of a growing plant

table.caption: Height of a plant, in centimeters, at week t, with the predictions of a linear model A and an exponential model B

items.q: Based on the residual plots, which model is more appropriate for the data, and why?
options: $L$, because its residuals are both positive and negative
$E$, because its residuals are small and show no pattern
$L$, because its residuals form a smooth curve
$E$, because its residuals are mostly above $0$

why.correct: An appropriate model leaves residuals scattered around $0$ with no pattern. The residuals of $L$ form a U: positive, then negative, then positive, which means the data bend away from the line. The residuals of $E$ stay near $0$ with no pattern.
options: Mixed signs are fine only without a pattern; these form a U.
Small, patternless residuals.
A curved pattern in the residuals is the sign of a poor model.
The residuals of $E$ are positive and negative.

items.q: The residual of $L$ at $t = 0$ is positive. What does that mean?
options: $L$ predicts more followers than the channel really had at $t = 0$
The channel gained followers at $t = 0$
$L$ predicts fewer followers than the channel had at $t = 0$
$L$ is increasing at $t = 0$

why.correct: Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted. A positive residual means actual $>$ predicted: the model underestimates there.
options: That is a negative residual, an overestimate.
A residual compares the model to the data; it is not a change in followers.
Actual minus predicted is positive: an underestimate.
The sign of a residual says nothing about whether the model is increasing.

items.q: Use exponential regression on the data to find $E(t) = ab^t$. What is the residual of $E$ at $t = 3$, correct to three decimal places?

mistakes.why: That is predicted minus actual. A residual is actual minus predicted.
That is the residual of the linear model $L$.

why.correct: Exponential regression gives $a = 210.015964...$ and $b = 1.250648...$. Then $E(3) = 410.825462...$, and the residual is actual $-$ predicted $= 410 - 410.825462... = -0.825462...$, about $-0.825$.

items.q: Use the stored exponential model $E$ to predict the number of followers at $t = 8$ weeks. Give the answer correct to three decimal places.

mistakes.why: That is the linear model's prediction. The residual plots favor $E$.

why.correct: $E(8) = ab^8 = 1256.991746...$ with the stored $a$ and $b$, about $1256.992$ followers.

items.q: Why does the U shape in the residuals of $L$ suggest that the data are not linear?
options: A U shape means the residuals add up to zero, so the line is wrong
Data above the line at the ends, below it in the middle: they curve up
A U shape means the follower counts are decreasing in the middle weeks
A U shape means the line is too steep at each of the weeks

why.correct: Positive residuals at the ends and negative ones in the middle mean the data lie above the line at the ends and below it in the middle: the data are concave up, which a line cannot follow.
options: Least-squares residuals of a line do add to zero, U or not; that is no evidence.
Data above, below, above the line: they curve up.
The data increase throughout; the residual is the gap to the line.
A slope that is too steep everywhere would give residuals with one trend, not a U.

items.q: What is the residual of model $A$ at $t = 3$?

mistakes.why: That is predicted minus actual. A residual is actual minus predicted.
That uses model $B$; the question asks about $A$.

why.correct: Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted $= 97 - 93 = 4$ cm. Model $A$ underestimates at $t = 3$.

items.q: What is the residual of model $B$ at $t = 1$?

mistakes.why: Subtract in the order actual minus predicted: $62 - 62.5$.

why.correct: $62 - 62.5 = -0.5$ cm. The negative residual means model $B$ overestimates at $t = 1$.

items.q: Which model fits the data in the table better, and why?
options: $B$, because its residuals are all closer to $0$
$A$, because it matches the data exactly at $t = 2$
$A$, because its residuals are whole numbers
$B$, because its predictions are larger

why.correct: The residuals of $A$ are $2, -1, 0, 4$; those of $B$ are $0, -0.5, -0.1, -0.7$. Every residual of $B$ is at least as close to $0$, and the largest error of $B$ ($0.7$ cm) is smaller than the largest of $A$ ($4$ cm).
options: Smaller errors at each time.
One exact match does not outweigh larger errors elsewhere.
Whole numbers are not a measure of fit.
Larger predictions are better only where the model underestimates.

items.q: The residuals of model $B$ are $0, -0.5, -0.1, -0.7$. What do the negative residuals say?
options: $B$ slightly underestimates the height at those weeks
$B$ slightly overestimates the height at those weeks
The plant shrank at those weeks
$B$ is decreasing at those weeks

why.correct: A negative residual means actual $<$ predicted, so the model predicts a little more than the real height.
options: Underestimates give positive residuals.
Predicted more than actual.
The actual heights increase each week.
A residual compares a prediction with the data.

items.q: How is a residual defined in this course?
options: Predicted value minus actual value
Actual value divided by predicted value
Actual value minus predicted value
The difference between two predictions

why.correct: A residual is actual minus predicted. The error of a prediction can be stated as predicted minus actual, or as the absolute value of the difference.
options: This is the opposite sign; it is the error of the prediction, not the residual.
A residual is a difference, not a ratio.
Positive when the model underestimates.
A residual compares a prediction with data.

items.q: Which features of a residual plot suggest that a model is appropriate for the data? Select all that apply.
options: The residuals are scattered above and below $0$ with no pattern
The residuals stay above $0$ across the inputs
The residuals form a curved pattern
The residuals grow steadily larger as the input increases

why.correct: A good model leaves only small, patternless residuals. A curve or a steady trend in the residuals shows the model misses the shape of the data.
options: No pattern: the model captures the shape.
Residuals of one sign mean the model underestimates throughout: a pattern.
A curve means the data bend away from the model.
A trend means the error grows in a predictable way.

items.q: A model predicts a tide height of $3.2$ m at noon, and the measured height is $2.9$ m. What is the residual at noon?

mistakes.why: That is predicted minus actual. The residual is $2.9 - 3.2$.
That adds the two heights; subtract them.

why.correct: Residual $=$ actual $-$ predicted $= 2.9 - 3.2 = -0.3$ m. The model overestimates at noon.

items.q: A model predicts $142$ visitors, and $150$ visitors come. What is the absolute error of the prediction?

mistakes.why: The absolute error is the size of the difference, so it is not negative.
That adds the two values; subtract them.

items.q: On $3 \le t \le 6$, every residual of a model is positive. Which statement is supported?
options: The model overestimates on $3 \le t \le 6$
The model is increasing over the interval $3 \le t \le 6$
The model underestimates on $3 \le t \le 6$
The model is a good fit on $3 \le t \le 6$

why.correct: Positive residuals mean actual $>$ predicted throughout the interval: the model underestimates there.
options: Overestimates give negative residuals.
Residual signs do not describe the model's direction.
Actual above predicted.
Residuals with one sign over an interval are a pattern, which suggests a poorer fit there.

items.q: A linear model's residual plot is shaped like an upside-down U: negative, then positive, then negative. Which change to the model is most reasonable to try?
options: A linear model with a larger slope, so it rises faster
An exponential model with a base greater than $1$
The same linear model shifted up a few units
A concave-down model, such as a quadratic opening down

why.correct: Data above the line in the middle and below it at the ends bend downward: they are concave down. A concave-down model can follow that shape; an increasing exponential function is concave up.
options: A steeper line still cannot bend.
This is concave up, the wrong way.
Shifting moves every residual the same amount and keeps the pattern.
Match the concavity the residuals reveal.
